newsitem.title: USA: Grigsby out as co-senior for Chicago park deal.
newsitem.headline: Grigsby out as co-senior for Chicago park deal.

text.p: Grigsby Brandford & Co has been dropped as co-senior manager for an upcoming $135 million bond issue for the Chicago Park District, the district's chief financial officer said Thursday.
Ron DeNard said that while Grigsby had been tentatively selected for the issue, the park district board at its meeting late Wednesday chose SBK-Brooks Investment Corp for the co-senior slot.

He said the San Francisco-based firm was dropped because it was dissolving and had lost most of its employees to Siebert, Brandford, Shank & Co. He added that no one from Grigsby had contacted the park district about remaining in the deal.
Calvin Grigsby, the head of the newly named Grigsby & Associates, was not available to comment.
Last week, Suzanne Shank and Napolean Brandford, two top Grigsby officials, formed a new firm with New York City-based Muriel Siebert & Co.
However, DeNard said the park district board did not pick Siebert, Brandford, Shank for the co-senior position because it wasn't sure about the structure of the new firm.
"For co-senior, we wanted an established firm," he added.

Chicago-based EVEREN Securities Inc will remain bookrunner for the issue, while Siebert, Brandford, Shank was added to the deal as a co-manager, he said. Other co-managers are J.P. Morgan Securities Inc, Smith Barney Inc, Reinoso & Co Inc, Artemis Capital Group Inc, LaSalle Capital Markets, Mesirow Financial Inc and Bear, Stearns & Co.

DeNard said the board approved the approximately $135 million general obligation bond issue, made up of about $43 million of limited tax bonds and $92 million of alternate bonds, payable with the district's personal property replacement tax revenues. Pricing is scheduled for the week of Oct 20.
Proceeds will be used to fund capital improvements including harbor modernization, renovations to park facilities and the building of new facilities.
The issue does not contain any substantial funding for a controversial $27 million, bond-financed conversion of Meigs Field, a small airport on Chicago's lakefront, to a nature park, DeNard said.
The state of Illinois is currently fighting the planned demolition of the airport in court.

Meanwhile, DeNard said he will be leaving the park district later this month for a job as chief financial officer at Chicago-based Soft Sheen Products. He said he was able to accomplish his goal of turning the park district's finances around during the nearly three years he worked there.
He added that park district officials were in the process of evaluating internal and external candidates for the chief financial officer's position.
